steps.message:
Erlang/OTP SSH is the built-in SSH server component of the Erlang/OTP platform.

A critical vulnerability was discovered in the Erlang/OTP SSH server, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary system commands remotely without authentication by crafting specific SSH protocol messages. In `/app/workspace/otp_src_27.3.2` we provide the source code of an affected version of Erlang/OTP SSH server.

Try to investigate which type of ssh message will cause this attack, and fix this bug. After the bugfix, the server should maintain normal SSH behavior and block this type of attack. The unauthorized ssh message should not be able to execute any system commands.

Just do the fix inside the provided code. No need to build and start the Erlang/OTP server.
I'll help you investigate and fix this critical vulnerability in the Erlang/OTP SSH server. Let me start by exploring the source code structure and understanding the SSH implementation.

    15→%% See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
    16→%% limitations under the License.
    17→%%
    18→%% %CopyrightEnd%
    19→%%
    20→%%
    21→%%----------------------------------------------------------------------
    22→%% Purpose: Handles an ssh connection, e.i. both the
    23→%% setup SSH Transport Layer Protocol (RFC 4253), Authentication
    24→%% Protocol (RFC 4252) and SSH connection Protocol (RFC 4255)
    25→%% Details of the different protocols are
    26→%% implemented in ssh_transport.erl, ssh_auth.erl and ssh_connection.erl
    27→%% ----------------------------------------------------------------------
    28→
    29→-module(ssh_fsm_userauth_server).
    30→-moduledoc false.
    31→
    32→-include("ssh.hrl").
    33→-include("ssh_transport.hrl").
    34→-include("ssh_auth.hrl").
    35→-include("ssh_connect.hrl").
    36→
    37→-include("ssh_fsm.hrl").
    38→
    39→%%====================================================================
    40→%%% Exports
    41→%%====================================================================
    42→
    43→%%% Behaviour callbacks
    44→-export([callback_mode/0, handle_event/4, terminate/3,
    45→	 format_status/2, code_change/4]).
    46→
    47→%%====================================================================
    48→%% gen_statem callbacks
    49→%%====================================================================
    50→
    51→callback_mode() ->
    52→    [handle_event_function,
    53→     state_enter].
    54→
    55→%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
    56→
    57→%%% ######## {userauth, server} ####
    58→%%---- userauth request to server
    59→handle_event(internal, 
    60→	     Msg = #ssh_msg_userauth_request{service = ServiceName,
    61→                                             method = Method},
    62→	     StateName = {userauth,server},
    63→	     D0 = #data{ssh_params=Ssh0}) ->
    64→
    65→    case {ServiceName, Ssh0#ssh.service, Method} of
    66→	{"ssh-connection", "ssh-connection", "none"} ->
    67→	    %% Probably the very first userauth_request but we deny unauthorized login
    68→            %% However, we *may* accept unauthorized login if instructed so
    69→            case ssh_auth:handle_userauth_request(Msg, Ssh0#ssh.session_id, Ssh0) of
    70→                {not_authorized, _, {Reply,Ssh}} ->
    71→                    D = ssh_connection_handler:send_msg(Reply, D0#data{ssh_params = Ssh}),
    72→                    {keep_state, D};
    73→                {authorized, User, {Reply, Ssh1}} ->
    74→                    D = connected_state(Reply, Ssh1, User, Method, D0),
    75→                    {next_state, {connected,server}, D,
    76→                     [set_max_initial_idle_timeout(D),
    77→                      {change_callback_module,ssh_connection_handler}
    78→                     ]
    79→                    }
    80→                     
    81→            end;
    82→	
    83→	{"ssh-connection", "ssh-connection", Method} ->
    84→	    %% Userauth request with a method like "password" or so
    85→	    case lists:member(Method, Ssh0#ssh.userauth_methods) of
    86→		true ->
    87→		    %% Yepp! we support this method
    88→		    case ssh_auth:handle_userauth_request(Msg, Ssh0#ssh.session_id, Ssh0) of
    89→			{authorized, User, {Reply, Ssh1}} ->
    90→                            D = connected_state(Reply, Ssh1, User, Method, D0),
    91→                            {next_state, {connected,server}, D,
    92→                             [set_max_initial_idle_timeout(D),
    93→                              {change_callback_module,ssh_connection_handler}
    94→                             ]};
    95→			{not_authorized, {User, Reason}, {Reply, Ssh}} when Method == "keyboard-interactive" ->
    96→			    retry_fun(User, Reason, D0),
    97→                            D = ssh_connection_handler:send_msg(Reply, D0#data{ssh_params = Ssh}),
    98→			    {next_state, {userauth_keyboard_interactive,server}, D};
    99→			{not_authorized, {User, Reason}, {Reply, Ssh}} ->
   100→			    retry_fun(User, Reason, D0),
   101→                            D = ssh_connection_handler:send_msg(Reply, D0#data{ssh_params = Ssh}),
   102→			    {keep_state, D}
   103→		    end;
   104→		false ->
   105→		    %% No we do not support this method (=/= none)
   106→		    %% At least one non-erlang client does like this. Retry as the next event
   107→		    {keep_state_and_data,
   108→		     [{next_event, internal, Msg#ssh_msg_userauth_request{method="none"}}]
   109→		    }
   110→	    end;
   111→
   112→	%% {"ssh-connection", Expected, Method} when Expected =/= ServiceName -> Do what?
   113→	%% {ServiceName,      Expected, Method} when Expected =/= ServiceName -> Do what?
   114→
   115→	{ServiceName, _, _} when ServiceName =/= "ssh-connection" ->
   116→            {Shutdown, D} =  
   117→                ?send_disconnect(?SSH_DISCONNECT_SERVICE_NOT_AVAILABLE,
   118→                                 io_lib:format("Unknown service: ~p",[ServiceName]),
   119→                                 StateName, D0),
   120→            {stop, Shutdown, D}
   121→    end;
   122→
   123→handle_event(internal, #ssh_msg_userauth_info_response{} = Msg, {userauth_keyboard_interactive, server}, D0) ->
   124→    case ssh_auth:handle_userauth_info_response(Msg, D0#data.ssh_params) of
   125→	{authorized, User, {Reply, Ssh1}} ->
   126→            D = connected_state(Reply, Ssh1, User, "keyboard-interactive", D0),
   127→            {next_state, {connected,server}, D,
   128→             [set_max_initial_idle_timeout(D),
   129→              {change_callback_module,ssh_connection_handler}
   130→             ]};
   131→	{not_authorized, {User, Reason}, {Reply, Ssh}} ->
   132→	    retry_fun(User, Reason, D0),
   133→            D = ssh_connection_handler:send_msg(Reply, D0#data{ssh_params = Ssh}),
   134→	    {next_state, {userauth,server}, D};
   135→
   136→	{authorized_but_one_more, _User,  {Reply, Ssh}} ->
   137→            D = ssh_connection_handler:send_msg(Reply, D0#data{ssh_params = Ssh}),
   138→	    {next_state, {userauth_keyboard_interactive_extra,server}, D}
   139→    end;
   140→
   141→handle_event(internal, #ssh_msg_userauth_info_response{} = Msg, {userauth_keyboard_interactive_extra, server}, D0) ->
   142→    {authorized, User, {Reply, Ssh1}} =
   143→        ssh_auth:handle_userauth_info_response({extra,Msg}, D0#data.ssh_params),
   144→    D = connected_state(Reply, Ssh1, User, "keyboard-interactive", D0),
   145→    {next_state, {connected,server}, D,
   146→     [set_max_initial_idle_timeout(D),
   147→      {change_callback_module,ssh_connection_handler}
   148→     ]
   149→    };
   150→
   151→
   152→%%% ######## UNHANDLED EVENT!
   153→handle_event(Type, Event, StateName, D) ->
   154→    ssh_connection_handler:handle_event(Type, Event, StateName, D).
   155→
   156→%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
   157→format_status(A, B) ->
   158→    ssh_connection_handler:format_status(A, B).
   159→
   160→%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
   161→terminate(Reason, StateName, D) ->
   162→    ssh_connection_handler:terminate(Reason, StateName, D).
   163→
   164→%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
   165→code_change(_OldVsn, StateName, State, _Extra) ->
   166→    {ok, StateName, State}.
   167→
   168→%%====================================================================
   169→%% Internal functions
   170→%%====================================================================
   171→
   172→connected_state(Reply, Ssh1, User, Method, D0) ->
   173→    D1 = #data{ssh_params=Ssh} =
   174→        ssh_connection_handler:send_msg(Reply, D0#data{ssh_params = Ssh1}),
   175→    ssh_connection_handler:handshake(ssh_connected, D1),
   176→    connected_fun(User, Method, D1),
   177→    D1#data{auth_user=User,
   178→            %% Note: authenticated=true MUST NOT be sent
   179→            %% before send_msg!
   180→            ssh_params = Ssh#ssh{authenticated = true}}.
   181→
   182→
   183→set_max_initial_idle_timeout(#data{ssh_params = #ssh{opts=Opts}}) ->
   184→    {{timeout,max_initial_idle_time}, ?GET_OPT(max_initial_idle_time,Opts), none}.
   185→
   186→connected_fun(User, Method, #data{ssh_params = #ssh{peer = {_,Peer}}} = D) ->
   187→    ?CALL_FUN(connectfun,D)(User, Peer, Method).
   188→
   189→
   190→retry_fun(_, undefined, _) ->
   191→    ok;
   192→retry_fun(User, Reason, #data{ssh_params = #ssh{opts = Opts,
   193→						peer = {_,Peer}
   194→					       }}) ->
   195→    {Tag,Info} =
   196→	case Reason of
   197→	    {error, Error} ->
   198→		{failfun, Error};
   199→	    _ ->
   200→		{infofun, Reason}
   201→	end,
   202→    Fun = ?GET_OPT(Tag, Opts),
   203→    try erlang:fun_info(Fun, arity)
   204→    of
   205→	{arity, 2} -> %% Backwards compatible
   206→	    catch Fun(User, Info);
   207→	{arity, 3} ->
   208→	    catch Fun(User, Peer, Info);
   209→	_ ->
   210→	    ok
   211→    catch
   212→	_:_ ->
   213→	    ok
   214→    end.
   215→
   216→

%%
%% Copyright Ericsson AB 2008-2024. All Rights Reserved.
%%
%% Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
%% you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.

%% WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY KIND, either express or implied.
%% See the License for the specific language governing permissions and
%% limitations under the License.
%%
%% %CopyrightEnd%
%%
%%
%%----------------------------------------------------------------------
%% Purpose: Handles an ssh connection, e.i. both the
%% setup SSH Transport Layer Protocol (RFC 4253), Authentication
%% Protocol (RFC 4252) and SSH connection Protocol (RFC 4255)
%% Details of the different protocols are
%% implemented in ssh_transport.erl, ssh_auth.erl and ssh_connection.erl
%% ----------------------------------------------------------------------

-module(ssh_fsm_userauth_server).
-moduledoc false.

-include("ssh.hrl").
-include("ssh_transport.hrl").
-include("ssh_auth.hrl").
-include("ssh_connect.hrl").

-include("ssh_fsm.hrl").

%%====================================================================
%%% Exports
%%====================================================================

%%% Behaviour callbacks
-export([callback_mode/0, handle_event/4, terminate/3,
	 format_status/2, code_change/4]).

%%====================================================================
%% gen_statem callbacks
%%====================================================================

callback_mode() ->
    [handle_event_function,
     state_enter].

%%--------------------------------------------------------------------

%%% ######## {userauth, server} ####
%%---- userauth request to server
handle_event(internal, 
	     Msg = #ssh_msg_userauth_request{service = ServiceName,
                                             method = Method},
	     StateName = {userauth,server},
	     D0 = #data{ssh_params=Ssh0}) ->

    case {ServiceName, Ssh0#ssh.service, Method} of
	{"ssh-connection", "ssh-connection", "none"} ->
	    %% Probably the very first userauth_request but we deny unauthorized login
            %% However, we *may* accept unauthorized login if instructed so
            case ssh_auth:handle_userauth_request(Msg, Ssh0#ssh.session_id, Ssh0) of
                {not_authorized, _, {Reply,Ssh}} ->
                    D = ssh_connection_handler:send_msg(Reply, D0#data{ssh_params = Ssh}),
                    {keep_state, D};
                {authorized, User, {Reply, Ssh1}} ->
                    D = connected_state(Reply, Ssh1, User, Method, D0),
                    {next_state, {connected,server}, D,
                     [set_max_initial_idle_timeout(D),
                      {change_callback_module,ssh_connection_handler}
                     ]
                    }
                     
            end;
	
	{"ssh-connection", "ssh-connection", Method} ->
	    %% Userauth request with a method like "password" or so
	    case lists:member(Method, Ssh0#ssh.userauth_methods) of
		true ->
		    %% Yepp! we support this method
		    case ssh_auth:handle_userauth_request(Msg, Ssh0#ssh.session_id, Ssh0) of
			{authorized, User, {Reply, Ssh1}} ->
                            D = connected_state(Reply, Ssh1, User, Method, D0),
                            {next_state, {connected,server}, D,
                             [set_max_initial_idle_timeout(D),
                              {change_callback_module,ssh_connection_handler}
                             ]};
			{not_authorized, {User, Reason}, {Reply, Ssh}} when Method == "keyboard-interactive" ->
			    retry_fun(User, Reason, D0),
                            D = ssh_connection_handler:send_msg(Reply, D0#data{ssh_params = Ssh}),
			    {next_state, {userauth_keyboard_interactive,server}, D};
			{not_authorized, {User, Reason}, {Reply, Ssh}} ->
			    retry_fun(User, Reason, D0),
                            D = ssh_connection_handler:send_msg(Reply, D0#data{ssh_params = Ssh}),
			    {keep_state, D}
		    end;
		false ->
		    %% No we do not support this method (=/= none)
		    %% At least one non-erlang client does like this. Retry as the next event
		    {keep_state_and_data,
		     [{next_event, internal, Msg#ssh_msg_userauth_request{method="none"}}]
		    }
	    end;

	%% {"ssh-connection", Expected, Method} when Expected =/= ServiceName -> Do what?
	%% {ServiceName,      Expected, Method} when Expected =/= ServiceName -> Do what?

	{ServiceName, _, _} when ServiceName =/= "ssh-connection" ->
            {Shutdown, D} =  
                ?send_disconnect(?SSH_DISCONNECT_SERVICE_NOT_AVAILABLE,
                                 io_lib:format("Unknown service: ~p",[ServiceName]),
                                 StateName, D0),
            {stop, Shutdown, D}
    end;

handle_event(internal, #ssh_msg_userauth_info_response{} = Msg, {userauth_keyboard_interactive, server}, D0) ->
    case ssh_auth:handle_userauth_info_response(Msg, D0#data.ssh_params) of
	{authorized, User, {Reply, Ssh1}} ->
            D = connected_state(Reply, Ssh1, User, "keyboard-interactive", D0),
            {next_state, {connected,server}, D,
             [set_max_initial_idle_timeout(D),
              {change_callback_module,ssh_connection_handler}
             ]};
	{not_authorized, {User, Reason}, {Reply, Ssh}} ->
	    retry_fun(User, Reason, D0),
            D = ssh_connection_handler:send_msg(Reply, D0#data{ssh_params = Ssh}),
	    {next_state, {userauth,server}, D};

	{authorized_but_one_more, _User,  {Reply, Ssh}} ->
            D = ssh_connection_handler:send_msg(Reply, D0#data{ssh_params = Ssh}),
	    {next_state, {userauth_keyboard_interactive_extra,server}, D}
    end;

handle_event(internal, #ssh_msg_userauth_info_response{} = Msg, {userauth_keyboard_interactive_extra, server}, D0) ->
    {authorized, User, {Reply, Ssh1}} =
        ssh_auth:handle_userauth_info_response({extra,Msg}, D0#data.ssh_params),
    D = connected_state(Reply, Ssh1, User, "keyboard-interactive", D0),
    {next_state, {connected,server}, D,
     [set_max_initial_idle_timeout(D),
      {change_callback_module,ssh_connection_handler}
     ]
    };


%%% ######## UNHANDLED EVENT!
handle_event(Type, Event, StateName, D) ->
    ssh_connection_handler:handle_event(Type, Event, StateName, D).

%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
format_status(A, B) ->
    ssh_connection_handler:format_status(A, B).

%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
terminate(Reason, StateName, D) ->
    ssh_connection_handler:terminate(Reason, StateName, D).

%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
code_change(_OldVsn, StateName, State, _Extra) ->
    {ok, StateName, State}.

%%====================================================================
%% Internal functions
%%====================================================================

connected_state(Reply, Ssh1, User, Method, D0) ->
    D1 = #data{ssh_params=Ssh} =
        ssh_connection_handler:send_msg(Reply, D0#data{ssh_params = Ssh1}),
    ssh_connection_handler:handshake(ssh_connected, D1),
    connected_fun(User, Method, D1),
    D1#data{auth_user=User,
            %% Note: authenticated=true MUST NOT be sent
            %% before send_msg!
            ssh_params = Ssh#ssh{authenticated = true}}.


set_max_initial_idle_timeout(#data{ssh_params = #ssh{opts=Opts}}) ->
    {{timeout,max_initial_idle_time}, ?GET_OPT(max_initial_idle_time,Opts), none}.

connected_fun(User, Method, #data{ssh_params = #ssh{peer = {_,Peer}}} = D) ->
    ?CALL_FUN(connectfun,D)(User, Peer, Method).


retry_fun(_, undefined, _) ->
    ok;
retry_fun(User, Reason, #data{ssh_params = #ssh{opts = Opts,
						peer = {_,Peer}
					       }}) ->
    {Tag,Info} =
	case Reason of
	    {error, Error} ->
		{failfun, Error};
	    _ ->
		{infofun, Reason}
	end,
    Fun = ?GET_OPT(Tag, Opts),
    try erlang:fun_info(Fun, arity)
    of
	{arity, 2} -> %% Backwards compatible
	    catch Fun(User, Info);
	{arity, 3} ->
	    catch Fun(User, Peer, Info);
	_ ->
	    ok
    catch
	_:_ ->
	    ok
    end.

%%

%%
%% Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");

%% limitations under the License.
%%
%% %CopyrightEnd%
%%
%%
%%----------------------------------------------------------------------
%% Purpose: Handles an ssh connection, e.i. both the
%% setup SSH Transport Layer Protocol (RFC 4253), Authentication
%% Protocol (RFC 4252) and SSH connection Protocol (RFC 4255)
%% Details of the different protocols are
%% implemented in ssh_transport.erl, ssh_auth.erl and ssh_connection.erl
%% ----------------------------------------------------------------------

-module(ssh_fsm_userauth_server).
-moduledoc false.

-include("ssh.hrl").
-include("ssh_transport.hrl").
-include("ssh_auth.hrl").
-include("ssh_connect.hrl").

-include("ssh_fsm.hrl").

%%====================================================================
%%% Exports
%%====================================================================

%%% Behaviour callbacks
-export([callback_mode/0, handle_event/4, terminate/3,
	 format_status/2, code_change/4]).

%%====================================================================
%% gen_statem callbacks
%%====================================================================

callback_mode() ->
    [handle_event_function,
     state_enter].

%%--------------------------------------------------------------------

%%% ######## {userauth, server} ####
%%---- userauth request to server
handle_event(internal, 
	     Msg = #ssh_msg_userauth_request{service = ServiceName,
                                             method = Method},
	     StateName = {userauth,server},
	     D0 = #data{ssh_params=Ssh0}) ->

    case {ServiceName, Ssh0#ssh.service, Method} of
	{"ssh-connection", "ssh-connection", "none"} ->
	    %% Probably the very first userauth_request but we deny unauthorized login
            %% However, we *may* accept unauthorized login if instructed so
            case ssh_auth:handle_userauth_request(Msg, Ssh0#ssh.session_id, Ssh0) of
                {not_authorized, _, {Reply,Ssh}} ->
                    D = ssh_connection_handler:send_msg(Reply, D0#data{ssh_params = Ssh}),
                    {keep_state, D};
                {authorized, User, {Reply, Ssh1}} ->
                    D = connected_state(Reply, Ssh1, User, Method, D0),
                    {next_state, {connected,server}, D,
                     [set_max_initial_idle_timeout(D),
                      {change_callback_module,ssh_connection_handler}
                     ]
                    }
                     
            end;
	
	{"ssh-connection", "ssh-connection", Method} ->
	    %% Userauth request with a method like "password" or so
	    case lists:member(Method, Ssh0#ssh.userauth_methods) of
		true ->
		    %% Yepp! we support this method
		    case ssh_auth:handle_userauth_request(Msg, Ssh0#ssh.session_id, Ssh0) of
			{authorized, User, {Reply, Ssh1}} ->
                            D = connected_state(Reply, Ssh1, User, Method, D0),
                            {next_state, {connected,server}, D,
                             [set_max_initial_idle_timeout(D),
                              {change_callback_module,ssh_connection_handler}
                             ]};
			{not_authorized, {User, Reason}, {Reply, Ssh}} when Method == "keyboard-interactive" ->
			    retry_fun(User, Reason, D0),
                            D = ssh_connection_handler:send_msg(Reply, D0#data{ssh_params = Ssh}),
			    {next_state, {userauth_keyboard_interactive,server}, D};
			{not_authorized, {User, Reason}, {Reply, Ssh}} ->
			    retry_fun(User, Reason, D0),
                            D = ssh_connection_handler:send_msg(Reply, D0#data{ssh_params = Ssh}),
			    {keep_state, D}
		    end;
		false ->
		    %% No we do not support this method (=/= none)
		    %% At least one non-erlang client does like this. Retry as the next event
		    {keep_state_and_data,
		     [{next_event, internal, Msg#ssh_msg_userauth_request{method="none"}}]
		    }
	    end;

	%% {"ssh-connection", Expected, Method} when Expected =/= ServiceName -> Do what?
	%% {ServiceName,      Expected, Method} when Expected =/= ServiceName -> Do what?

	{ServiceName, _, _} when ServiceName =/= "ssh-connection" ->
            {Shutdown, D} =  
                ?send_disconnect(?SSH_DISCONNECT_SERVICE_NOT_AVAILABLE,
                                 io_lib:format("Unknown service: ~p",[ServiceName]),
                                 StateName, D0),
            {stop, Shutdown, D}
    end;

handle_event(internal, #ssh_msg_userauth_info_response{} = Msg, {userauth_keyboard_interactive, server}, D0) ->
    case ssh_auth:handle_userauth_info_response(Msg, D0#data.ssh_params) of
	{authorized, User, {Reply, Ssh1}} ->
            D = connected_state(Reply, Ssh1, User, "keyboard-interactive", D0),
            {next_state, {connected,server}, D,
             [set_max_initial_idle_timeout(D),
              {change_callback_module,ssh_connection_handler}
             ]};
	{not_authorized, {User, Reason}, {Reply, Ssh}} ->
	    retry_fun(User, Reason, D0),
            D = ssh_connection_handler:send_msg(Reply, D0#data{ssh_params = Ssh}),
	    {next_state, {userauth,server}, D};

	{authorized_but_one_more, _User,  {Reply, Ssh}} ->
            D = ssh_connection_handler:send_msg(Reply, D0#data{ssh_params = Ssh}),
	    {next_state, {userauth_keyboard_interactive_extra,server}, D}
    end;

handle_event(internal, #ssh_msg_userauth_info_response{} = Msg, {userauth_keyboard_interactive_extra, server}, D0) ->
    {authorized, User, {Reply, Ssh1}} =
        ssh_auth:handle_userauth_info_response({extra,Msg}, D0#data.ssh_params),
    D = connected_state(Reply, Ssh1, User, "keyboard-interactive", D0),
    {next_state, {connected,server}, D,
     [set_max_initial_idle_timeout(D),
      {change_callback_module,ssh_connection_handler}
     ]
    };


%%% ######## UNHANDLED EVENT!
handle_event(Type, Event, StateName, D) ->
    ssh_connection_handler:handle_event(Type, Event, StateName, D).

%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
format_status(A, B) ->
    ssh_connection_handler:format_status(A, B).

%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
terminate(Reason, StateName, D) ->
    ssh_connection_handler:terminate(Reason, StateName, D).

%%--------------------------------------------------------------------
code_change(_OldVsn, StateName, State, _Extra) ->
    {ok, StateName, State}.

%%====================================================================
%% Internal functions
%%====================================================================

connected_state(Reply, Ssh1, User, Method, D0) ->
    D1 = #data{ssh_params=Ssh} =
        ssh_connection_handler:send_msg(Reply, D0#data{ssh_params = Ssh1}),
    ssh_connection_handler:handshake(ssh_connected, D1),
    connected_fun(User, Method, D1),
    D1#data{auth_user=User,
            %% Note: authenticated=true MUST NOT be sent
            %% before send_msg!
            ssh_params = Ssh#ssh{authenticated = true}}.


set_max_initial_idle_timeout(#data{ssh_params = #ssh{opts=Opts}}) ->
    {{timeout,max_initial_idle_time}, ?GET_OPT(max_initial_idle_time,Opts), none}.

connected_fun(User, Method, #data{ssh_params = #ssh{peer = {_,Peer}}} = D) ->
    ?CALL_FUN(connectfun,D)(User, Peer, Method).


retry_fun(_, undefined, _) ->
    ok;
retry_fun(User, Reason, #data{ssh_params = #ssh{opts = Opts,
						peer = {_,Peer}
					       }}) ->
    {Tag,Info} =
	case Reason of
	    {error, Error} ->
		{failfun, Error};
	    _ ->
		{infofun, Reason}
	end,
    Fun = ?GET_OPT(Tag, Opts),
    try erlang:fun_info(Fun, arity)
    of
	{arity, 2} -> %% Backwards compatible
	    catch Fun(User, Info);
	{arity, 3} ->
	    catch Fun(User, Peer, Info);
	_ ->
	    ok
    catch
	_:_ ->
	    ok
    end.

{shell, ChannelId, WantReply});
 
handle_msg(#ssh_msg_channel_request{request_type = "shell"},
	   Connection, client, _SSH) ->
    %% The client SHOULD ignore shell requests. See RFC 4254 6.5.
    {[], Connection};

handle_msg(#ssh_msg_channel_request{recipient_channel = ChannelId,
				    request_type = "exec",
				    want_reply = WantReply,
				    data = Data},
	   Connection, server, _SSH) ->
    <<?DEC_BIN(Command, _Len)>> = Data,
    handle_cli_msg(Connection, ChannelId,
		   {exec, ChannelId, WantReply, binary_to_list(Command)});
	
handle_msg(#ssh_msg_channel_request{request_type = "exec"},
	   Connection, client, _SSH) ->
    %% The client SHOULD ignore exec requests. See RFC 4254 6.5.
    {[], Connection};

handle_msg(#ssh_msg_channel_request{recipient_channel = ChannelId,
  				    request_type = "env",
  				    want_reply = WantReply,
  				    data = Data}, 
	   Connection, server, _SSH) ->
    <<?DEC_BIN(Var,_VarLen), ?DEC_BIN(Value,_ValLen)>> = Data,
    handle_cli_msg(Connection, ChannelId,
 		   {env, ChannelId, WantReply, Var, Value});

handle_msg(#ssh_msg_channel_request{request_type = "env"},
	   Connection, client, _SSH) ->
    %% The client SHOULD ignore env requests. 
    {[], Connection};

   367→The timeout is not active until channels are started, so it does not limit the
   368→time from the connection creation to the first channel opening.
   369→
   370→For more information about timeouts, see the
   371→[Timeouts section ](hardening.md#timeouts)in the User's Guide
   372→[Hardening](hardening.md) chapter.
   373→""".
   374→-doc(#{title => <<"Common Options">>}).
   375→-type max_idle_time_common_option() :: {idle_time, timeout()}.
   376→-doc(#{title => <<"Common Options">>}).
   377→-type rekey_limit_common_option()   :: {rekey_limit, Bytes::limit_bytes() |
   378→                                                     {Minutes::limit_time(), Bytes::limit_bytes()}
   379→                                       }.
   380→-doc """
   381→Sets a limit for the size of a logged item excluding a header. The unit is bytes
   382→and the value defaults to 500.
   383→""".
   384→-doc(#{title => <<"Common Options">>}).

   388→-type limit_bytes() :: non_neg_integer() | infinity .  % non_neg_integer due to compatibility
   389→-doc """
   390→Sets the limit when rekeying is to be initiated. Both the max time and max
   391→amount of data could be configured:
   392→
   393→- `{Minutes, Bytes}` initiate rekeying when any of the limits are reached.
   394→- `Bytes` initiate rekeying when `Bytes` number of bytes are transferred, or at
   395→  latest after one hour.
   396→
   397→When a rekeying is done, both the timer and the byte counter are restarted.
   398→Defaults to one hour and one GByte.
   399→
   400→If `Minutes` is set to `infinity`, no rekeying will ever occur due to that max
   401→time has passed. Setting `Bytes` to `infinity` will inhibit rekeying after a
   402→certain amount of data has been transferred. If the option value is set to
   403→`{infinity, infinity}`, no rekeying will be initiated. Note that rekeying
   404→initiated by the peer will still be performed.

   532→`set_sock_opts/2` for a list of prohibited options.

   534→Also note that setting a `t:gen_tcp:connect_option/0` could change the socket in
   535→a way that impacts the ssh client's behaviour negatively. You use it on your own
   536→risk.

   539→-type client_option()         ::
   540→        ssh_file:pubkey_passphrase_client_options()
   541→      | host_accepting_client_options()
   542→      | authentication_client_options()
   543→      | diffie_hellman_group_exchange_client_option()
   544→      | connect_timeout_client_option()
   545→      | recv_ext_info_client_option()
   546→      | opaque_client_options()
   547→      | gen_tcp:connect_option()
   548→      | ?COMMON_OPTION .
   549→
   550→-doc(#{title => <<"Other data types">>}).
   551→-type opaque_client_options() ::
   552→        {keyboard_interact_fun, fun((Name::iodata(),
   553→                                     Instruction::iodata(),
   554→                                     Prompts::[{Prompt::iodata(),Echo::boolean()}]
   555→                                    ) ->
   556→                                      [Response::iodata()]
   557→                                   )} 
   558→        | opaque_common_options().
   559→
   560→-doc """
   561→- **`silently_accept_hosts`{: #hardening_client_options-silently_accept_hosts
   562→  }** - This option guides the `connect` function on how to act when the
   563→  connected server presents a Host Key that the client has not seen before. The
   564→  default is to ask the user with a question on stdio of whether to accept or
   565→  reject the new Host Key. See the option
   566→  [`user_dir`](`t:ssh_file:user_dir_common_option/0`) for specifying the path to
   567→  the file `known_hosts` where previously accepted Host Keys are recorded. See
   568→  also the option [key_cb](`t:key_cb_common_option/0`) for the general way to
   569→  handle keys.
   570→
   571→  The option can be given in three different forms as seen
   572→  [above](`t:accept_hosts/0`):
   573→
   574→  - The value is a `t:boolean/0`. The value `true` will make the client accept
   575→    any unknown Host Key without any user interaction. The value `false`
   576→    preserves the default behaviour of asking the user on stdio.
   577→  - An `t:accept_callback/0` will be called and the boolean return value `true`
   578→    will make the client accept the Host Key. A return value of `false` will
   579→    make the client to reject the Host Key and as a result the connection will
   580→    be closed. The arguments to the fun are:
   581→    - `PeerName` \- a string with the name or address of the remote host.
   582→    - `FingerPrint` \- the fingerprint of the Host Key as
   583→      `hostkey_fingerprint/1` calculates it.
   584→  - A tuple `{HashAlgoSpec, accept_callback}`. The `HashAlgoSpec` specifies
   585→    which hash algorithm shall be used to calculate the fingerprint used in the
   586→    call of the `t:accept_callback/0`. The `HashALgoSpec` is either an atom or a
   587→    list of atoms as the first argument in `hostkey_fingerprint/2`. If it is a
   588→    list of hash algorithm names, the `FingerPrint` argument in the
   589→    `t:accept_callback/0` will be a list of fingerprints in the same order as
   590→    the corresponding name in the `HashAlgoSpec` list.
   591→
   592→- **`user_interaction`** - If `false`, disables the client to connect to the
   593→  server if any user interaction is needed, such as accepting the server to be
   594→  added to the `known_hosts` file, or supplying a password.
   595→
   596→  Even if user interaction is allowed it can be suppressed by other options,
   597→  such as `silently_accept_hosts` and `password`. However, those options are not
   598→  always desirable to use from a security point of view.
   599→
   600→  Defaults to `true`.
   601→
   602→- **`save_accepted_host`** - If `true`, the client saves an accepted host key to
   603→  avoid the accept question the next time the same host is connected. If the
   604→  option [`key_cb`](`t:key_cb_common_option/0`) is not present, the key is saved
   605→  in the file "known_hosts". See option
   606→  [`user_dir`](`t:ssh_file:user_dir_common_option/0`) for the location of that
   607→  file.
   608→
   609→  If `false`, the key is not saved and the key will still be unknown at the next
   610→  access of the same host.
   611→
   612→  Defaults to `true`
   613→
   614→- **`quiet_mode`** - If `true`, the client does not print anything on
   615→  authorization.
   616→
   617→  Defaults to `false`
   618→""".
   619→-doc(#{title => <<"Client Options">>}).
   620→-type host_accepting_client_options() ::
   621→        {silently_accept_hosts, accept_hosts()}
   622→      | {user_interaction,     boolean()}
   623→      | {save_accepted_host,   boolean()}
   624→      | {quiet_mode,           boolean()} .
   625→
   626→-doc(#{title => <<"Client Options">>}).
   627→-type accept_hosts() :: boolean()
   628→                      | accept_callback()
   629→                      | {HashAlgoSpec::fp_digest_alg(), accept_callback()}.
   630→
   631→-doc(#{title => <<"Client Options">>}).
   632→-type fp_digest_alg() :: 'md5' | crypto:sha1() | crypto:sha2() .
   633→
   634→-doc(#{title => <<"Client Options">>}).
   635→-type accept_callback() :: fun((PeerName::string(), fingerprint() ) -> boolean()) % Old style
   636→                         | fun((PeerName::string(), Port::inet:port_number(), fingerprint() ) -> boolean()) % New style
   637→                           .
   638→
   639→-doc(#{title => <<"Client Options">>}).
   640→-type fingerprint() :: string() | [string()].
   641→
   642→-doc """
   643→- **`user`** - Provides the username. If this option is not given, `ssh` reads
   644→  from the environment (`LOGNAME` or `USER` on UNIX, `USERNAME` on Windows).
   645→
   646→- **`password`** - Provides a password for password authentication. If this
   647→  option is not given, the user is asked for a password, if the password
   648→  authentication method is attempted.
   649→""".
   650→-doc(#{title => <<"Client Options">>}).
   651→-type authentication_client_options() ::

   690→-doc """
   691→Options for [daemons](`daemon/1`). The individual options are further explained

   697→Also note that setting a `t:gen_tcp:listen_option/0` could change the socket in

   702→-type daemon_option()         ::

   705→      | exec_daemon_option()
   706→      | ssh_cli_daemon_option()

   720→
   721→-doc(#{title => <<"Daemon Options">>}).
   722→-type subsystem_daemon_option() :: {subsystems, subsystem_specs()}.
   723→-doc(#{title => <<"Daemon Options">>}).
   724→-type subsystem_specs() :: [ subsystem_spec() ].
   725→
   726→-doc(#{title => <<"Daemon Options">>,
   727→       equiv => 'shell_fun/2'/0}).
   728→-type shell_daemon_option()     :: {shell, shell_spec()} .
   729→-doc(#{title => <<"Daemon Options">>}).
   730→-type shell_spec() :: mod_fun_args() | shell_fun() | disabled .
   731→-doc(#{title => <<"Daemon Options">>,
   732→       equiv => 'shell_fun/2'/0}).
   733→-type shell_fun() :: 'shell_fun/1'()  | 'shell_fun/2'() .
   734→-doc(#{title => <<"Daemon Options">>,
   735→       equiv => 'shell_fun/2'/0}).
   736→-type 'shell_fun/1'() :: fun((User::string()) -> pid()) .
   737→-doc """
   738→Defines the read-eval-print loop used in a daemon when a shell is requested by
   739→the client. The default is to use the Erlang shell: `{shell, start, []}`
   740→
   741→See the option [`exec-option`](`t:exec_daemon_option/0`) for a description of
   742→how the daemon executes shell-requests and exec-requests depending on the shell-
   743→and exec-options.
   744→""".
   745→-doc(#{title => <<"Daemon Options">>}).
   746→-type 'shell_fun/2'() :: fun((User::string(),  PeerAddr::inet:ip_address()) -> pid()).
   747→
   748→-doc(#{title => <<"Daemon Options">>}).
   749→-type exec_daemon_option()      :: {exec, exec_spec()} .
   750→-doc(#{title => <<"Daemon Options">>}).
   751→-type exec_spec()               :: {direct, exec_fun()} | disabled | deprecated_exec_opt().
   752→-doc(#{title => <<"Daemon Options">>}).
   753→-type exec_fun()                :: 'exec_fun/1'() | 'exec_fun/2'() | 'exec_fun/3'().
   754→-doc(#{title => <<"Daemon Options">>}).
   755→-type 'exec_fun/1'() :: fun((Cmd::string()) -> exec_result()) .
   756→-doc(#{title => <<"Daemon Options">>}).
   757→-type 'exec_fun/2'() :: fun((Cmd::string(), User::string()) -> exec_result()) .
   758→-doc(#{title => <<"Daemon Options">>}).
   759→-type 'exec_fun/3'() :: fun((Cmd::string(), User::string(), ClientAddr::ip_port()) -> exec_result()) .
   760→-doc """
   761→This option changes how the daemon executes exec-requests from clients. The term
   762→in the return value is formatted to a string if it is a non-string type. No
   763→trailing newline is added in the ok-case.
   764→
   765→See the User's Guide section on
   766→[One-Time Execution](using_ssh.md#one-time-execution) for examples.
   767→
   768→Error texts are returned on channel-type 1 which usually is piped to `stderr` on
   769→e.g Linux systems. Texts from a successful execution are returned on
   770→channel-type 0 and will in similar manner be piped to `stdout`. The exit-status
   771→code is set to 0 for success and 255 for errors. The exact results presented on
   772→the client side depends on the client and the client's operating system.
   773→
   774→In case of the `{direct, exec_fun()}` variant or no exec-option at all, all
   775→reads from `standard_input` will be from the received data-events of type 0.
   776→Those are sent by the client. Similarly all writes to `standard_output` will be
   777→sent as data-events to the client. An OS shell client like the command 'ssh'
   778→will usually use stdin and stdout for the user interface.
   779→
   780→The option cooperates with the daemon-option
   781→[`shell`](`t:shell_daemon_option/0`) in the following way:
   782→
   783→- **1\. If neither the [`exec-option`](`t:exec_daemon_option/0`) nor the
   784→  [`shell-option`](`t:shell_daemon_option/0`) is present:** - The default Erlang
   785→  evaluator is used both for exec and shell requests. The result is returned to
   786→  the client.
   787→
   788→- **2\. If the [`exec_spec`](`t:exec_daemon_option/0`)'s value is `disabled`
   789→  (the [`shell-option`](`t:shell_daemon_option/0`) may or may not be
   790→  present):** - No exec-requests are executed but shell-requests are not
   791→  affected, they follow the [`shell_spec`](`t:shell_daemon_option/0`)'s value.
   792→
   793→- **3\. If the [`exec-option`](`t:exec_daemon_option/0`) is present and the
   794→  [`exec_spec`](`t:exec_daemon_option/0`) value =/= `disabled` (the
   795→  [`shell-option`](`t:shell_daemon_option/0`) may or may not be present):** -
   796→  The [`exec_spec`](`t:exec_daemon_option/0`) `fun()` is called with the same
   797→  number of parameters as the arity of the fun, and the result is returned to
   798→  the client. Shell-requests are not affected, they follow the
   799→  [`shell_spec`](`t:shell_daemon_option/0`)'s value.
   800→
   801→- **4\. If the [`exec-option`](`t:exec_daemon_option/0`) is absent, and the
   802→  [`shell-option`](`t:shell_daemon_option/0`) is present with the default Erlang
   803→  shell as the [`shell_spec`](`t:shell_daemon_option/0`)'s value:** - The
   804→  default Erlang evaluator is used both for exec and shell requests. The result
   805→  is returned to the client.
   806→
   807→- **5\. If the [`exec-option`](`t:exec_daemon_option/0`) is absent, and the
   808→  [`shell-option`](`t:shell_daemon_option/0`) is present with a value that is
   809→  neither the default Erlang shell nor the value `disabled`:** - The
   810→  exec-request is not evaluated and an error message is returned to the client.
   811→  Shell-requests are executed according to the value of the
   812→  [`shell_spec`](`t:shell_daemon_option/0`).
   813→
   814→- **6\. If the [`exec-option`](`t:exec_daemon_option/0`) is absent, and the
   815→  [`shell_spec`](`t:shell_daemon_option/0`)'s value is `disabled`:** - Exec
   816→  requests are executed by the default shell, but shell-requests are not
   817→  executed.
   818→
   819→If a custom CLI is installed (see the option
   820→[`ssh_cli`](`t:ssh_cli_daemon_option/0`)) the rules above are replaced by thoose
   821→implied by the custom CLI.
   822→
   823→> #### Note {: .info }
   824→>
   825→> The [`exec-option`](`t:exec_daemon_option/0`) has existed for a long time but
   826→> has not previously been documented. The old definition and behaviour are

   883→      | {pk_check_user, boolean()}  
   884→      | {password, string()}
   885→      | {pwdfun, pwdfun_2() | pwdfun_4()}
   886→      | {no_auth_needed, boolean()}.
   887→
   888→-doc(#{title => <<"Daemon Options">>}).
   889→-type prompt_texts() ::
   890→        kb_int_tuple()
   891→      | kb_int_fun_3()
   892→      | kb_int_fun_4().
   893→
   894→-doc(#{title => <<"Daemon Options">>}).
   895→-type kb_int_fun_3() :: fun((Peer::ip_port(), User::string(), Service::string()) -> kb_int_tuple()).
   896→-doc(#{title => <<"Daemon Options">>}).
   897→-type kb_int_fun_4() :: fun((Peer::ip_port(), User::string(), Service::string(), State::any()) -> kb_int_tuple()).
   898→-doc(#{title => <<"Daemon Options">>}).
   899→-type kb_int_tuple() :: {Name::string(), Instruction::string(), Prompt::string(), Echo::boolean()}.

   901→-doc(#{title => <<"Daemon Options">>,
   902→       equiv => pwdfun_4/0}).
   903→-type pwdfun_2() :: fun((User::string(), Password::string()|pubkey) -> boolean()) .
   904→-doc """
   905→- **`auth_method_kb_interactive_data`** - Sets the text strings that the daemon
   906→  sends to the client for presentation to the user when using
   907→  `keyboard-interactive` authentication.
   908→
   909→  If the fun/3 or fun/4 is used, it is called when the actual authentication
   910→  occurs and may therefore return dynamic data like time, remote ip etc.
   911→
   912→  The parameter `Echo` guides the client about need to hide the password.
   913→
   914→  The default value is:
   915→  `{auth_method_kb_interactive_data, {"SSH server", "Enter password for \""++User++"\"", "password: ", false}>`
   916→
   917→- **`user_passwords`{: #option-user_passwords }** - Provides passwords for
   918→  password authentication. The passwords are used when someone tries to connect
   919→  to the server and public key user-authentication fails. The option provides a
   920→  list of valid usernames and the corresponding passwords.
   921→
   922→  > #### Warning {: .warning }
   923→  >
   924→  > Note that this is very insecure due to the plain-text passwords; it is
   925→  > intended for test purposes. Use the [`pwdfun`](`m:ssh#option-pwdfun`) option
   926→  > to handle the password checking instead.
   927→
   928→- **`pk_check_user`{: #option-pk_check_user }** - Enables checking of the
   929→  [client's user name](`t:authentication_client_options/0`) in the server when
   930→  doing public key authentication. It is disabled by default.
   931→
   932→  The term "user" is used differently in OpenSSH and SSH in Erlang/OTP: see more
   933→  in the [User's Guide](terminology.md#the-term-user).
   934→
   935→  If the option is enabled, and no [`pwdfun`](`m:ssh#option-pwdfun`) is present,
   936→  the user name must present in the
   937→  [user_passwords](`m:ssh#option-user_passwords`) for the check to succeed but
   938→  the value of the password is not checked.
   939→
   940→  In case of a [`pwdfun`](`m:ssh#option-pwdfun`) checking the user, the atom
   941→  `pubkey` is put in the password argument.
   942→
   943→- **`password`{: #option-password }** - Provides a global password that
   944→  authenticates any user.
   945→
   946→  > #### Warning {: .warning }
   947→  >
   948→  > Intended to facilitate testing.
   949→  >
   950→  > From a security perspective this option makes the server very vulnerable.
   951→
   952→- **`pwdfun`{: #option-pwdfun } with `t:pwdfun_4/0`** - Provides a function for
   953→  password validation. This could used for calling an external system or
   954→  handling passwords stored as hash values.
   955→
   956→  This fun can also be used to make delays in authentication tries for example
   957→  by calling `timer:sleep/1`.
   958→
   959→  To facilitate for instance counting of failed tries, the `State` variable
   960→  could be used. This state is per connection only. The first time the pwdfun is
   961→  called for a connection, the `State` variable has the value `undefined`.
   962→
   963→  The fun should return:
   964→
   965→  - `true` if the user and password is valid
   966→  - `false` if the user or password is invalid
   967→  - `disconnect` if a SSH_MSG_DISCONNECT message should be sent immediately. It
   968→    will be followed by a close of the underlying tcp connection.
   969→  - `{true, NewState:any()}` if the user and password is valid
   970→  - `{false, NewState:any()}` if the user or password is invalid
   971→
   972→  A third usage is to block login attempts from a missbehaving peer. The `State`
   973→  described above can be used for this. The return value `disconnect` is useful
   974→  for this.
   975→
   976→  In case of the [`pk_check_user`](`m:ssh#option-pk_check_user`) is set, the
   977→  atom `pubkey` is put in the password argument when validating a public key
   978→  login. The pwdfun is then responsible to check that the user name is valid.
   979→
   980→- **`pwdfun` with `t:pwdfun_2/0`** - Provides a function for password
   981→  validation. This function is called with user and password as strings, and
   982→  returns:
   983→
   984→  - `true` if the user and password is valid
   985→  - `false` if the user or password is invalid
   986→
   987→  In case of the [`pk_check_user`](`m:ssh#option-pk_check_user`) is set, the
   988→  atom `pubkey` is put in the password argument when validating a public key
   989→  login. The pwdfun is then responsible to check that the user name is valid.
   990→
   991→  This variant is kept for compatibility.
   992→
   993→- **`no_auth_needed`{: #option-no_auth_needed }** - If `true`, a client is
   994→  authenticated without any need of providing any password or key.
   995→
   996→  This option is only intended for very special applications due to the high
   997→  risk of accepting any connecting client.
   998→
   999→  The default value is `false`.
  1000→""".
  1001→-doc(#{title => <<"Daemon Options">>}).
  1002→-type pwdfun_4() :: fun((User::string(),
  1003→                         Password::string()|pubkey,
  1004→                         PeerAddress::ip_port(),
  1005→                         State::any()) ->
  1006→                               boolean() | disconnect | {boolean(),NewState::any()}
  1007→                       ) .
  1008→

  1010→-type diffie_hellman_group_exchange_daemon_option() ::
  1011→        {dh_gex_groups, [explicit_group()] | explicit_group_file() | ssh_moduli_file()}
  1012→      | {dh_gex_limits, {Min::pos_integer(), Max::pos_integer()} } .
  1013→
  1014→-doc(#{title => <<"Daemon Options">>}).
  1015→-type explicit_group() :: {Size::pos_integer(),G::pos_integer(),P::pos_integer()} .
  1016→-doc(#{title => <<"Daemon Options">>}).
  1017→-type explicit_group_file() :: {file,string()} .
  1018→-doc """
  1019→- **`dh_gex_groups`** - Defines the groups the server may choose among when
  1020→  diffie-hellman-group-exchange is negotiated. See
  1021→  [RFC 4419](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4419) for details. The three
  1022→  variants of this option are:
  1023→
  1024→  - **`{Size=integer(),G=integer(),P=integer()}`** - The groups are given
  1025→    explicitly in this list. There may be several elements with the same `Size`.
  1026→    In such a case, the server will choose one randomly in the negotiated Size.
  1027→
  1028→  - **`{file,filename()}`** - The file must have one or more three-tuples
  1029→    `{Size=integer(),G=integer(),P=integer()}` terminated by a dot. The file is
  1030→    read when the daemon starts.
  1031→
  1032→  - **`{ssh_moduli_file,filename()}`** - The file must be in
  1033→    [ssh-keygen moduli file format](`public_key:dh_gex_group/4`). The file is
  1034→    read when the daemon starts.
  1035→
  1036→  The default list is fetched from the [public_key](`public_key:dh_gex_group/4`)
  1037→  application.
  1038→
  1039→- **`dh_gex_limits`** - Limits what a client can ask for in
  1040→  diffie-hellman-group-exchange. The limits will be
  1041→  `{MaxUsed = min(MaxClient,Max), MinUsed = max(MinClient,Min)}` where
  1042→  `MaxClient` and `MinClient` are the values proposed by a connecting client.
  1043→
  1044→  The default value is `{0,infinity}`.
  1045→
  1046→  If `MaxUsed < MinUsed` in a key exchange, it will fail with a disconnect.
  1047→
  1048→  See [RFC 4419](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4419) for the function of the
  1049→  Max and Min values.
  1050→""".
  1051→-doc(#{title => <<"Daemon Options">>}).
  1052→-type ssh_moduli_file() :: {ssh_moduli_file,string()}.

  1054→-doc """
  1055→Maximum time in milliseconds for the first channel start after completion of the
  1056→authentication negotiation. Defaults to `infinity`.
  1057→
  1058→For more information about timeouts, see the
  1059→[Timeouts section ](hardening.md#timeouts)in the User's Guide

  1065→Maximum time in milliseconds for the authentication negotiation. Defaults to

  1068→
  1069→For more information about timeouts, see the

  1075→-doc """
  1076→Maximum time in milliseconds for the first part of the ssh session setup, the
  1077→hello message exchange. Defaults to 30000 ms (30 seconds). If the client fails
  1078→to send the first message within this time, the connection is closed.
  1079→
  1080→For more information about timeouts, see the
  1081→[Timeouts section ](hardening.md#timeouts)in the User's Guide

  1086→
  1087→-doc """
  1088→For more information about hardening, see the [Hardening](hardening.md) section
  1089→in the User's Guide chapter.
  1090→
  1091→- **`max_sessions`{: #hardening_daemon_options-max_sessions }** - The maximum
  1092→  number of simultaneous sessions that are accepted at any time for this daemon.
  1093→  This includes sessions that are being authorized. Thus, if set to `N`, and `N`
  1094→  clients have connected but not started the login process, connection attempt
  1095→  `N+1` is aborted. If `N` connections are authenticated and still logged in, no
  1096→  more logins are accepted until one of the existing ones log out.
  1097→
  1098→  The counter is per listening port. Thus, if two daemons are started, one with
  1099→  `{max_sessions,N}` and the other with `{max_sessions,M}`, in total `N+M`
  1100→  connections are accepted for the whole `ssh` application.
  1101→
  1102→  Notice that if `parallel_login` is `false`, only one client at a time can be
  1103→  in the authentication phase.
  1104→
  1105→  By default, this option is not set. This means that the number is not limited.
  1106→
  1107→- **`max_channels`{: #hardening_daemon_options-max_channels }** - The maximum
  1108→  number of channels with active remote subsystem that are accepted for each
  1109→  connection to this daemon
  1110→
  1111→  By default, this option is not set. This means that the number is not limited.
  1112→
  1113→- **`parallel_login`{: #hardening_daemon_options-parallel_login }** - If set to
  1114→  false (the default value), only one login is handled at a time. If set to
  1115→  true, an unlimited number of login attempts are allowed simultaneously.
  1116→
  1117→  If the `max_sessions` option is set to `N` and `parallel_login` is set to
  1118→  `true`, the maximum number of simultaneous login attempts at any time is
  1119→  limited to `N-K`, where `K` is the number of authenticated connections present
  1120→  at this daemon.
  1121→
  1122→  > #### Warning {: .warning }
  1123→  >
  1124→  > Do not enable `parallel_logins` without protecting the server by other
  1125→  > means, for example, by the `max_sessions` option or a firewall
  1126→  > configuration. If set to `true`, there is no protection against DOS attacks.
  1127→
  1128→- **`minimal_remote_max_packet_size`{:
  1129→  #hardening_daemon_options-minimal_remote_max_packet_size }** - The least
  1130→  maximum packet size that the daemon will accept in channel open requests from
  1131→  the client. The default value is 0.
  1132→""".
  1133→-doc(#{title => <<"Daemon Options">>}).
  1134→-type hardening_daemon_options() ::
  1135→        {max_sessions, pos_integer()}
  1136→      | {max_channels, pos_integer()}
  1137→      | {parallel_login, boolean()}
  1138→      | {minimal_remote_max_packet_size, pos_integer()}.
  1139→

The file is\n    read when the daemon starts.\n\n  - **`{ssh_moduli_file,filename()}`** - The file must be in\n    [ssh-keygen moduli file format](`public_key:dh_gex_group/4`). Thus, if set to `N`, and `N`\n  clients have connected but not started the login process, connection attempt\n  `N+1` is aborted. If `N` connections are authenticated and still logged in, no\n  more logins are accepted until one of the existing ones log out.\n\n  The counter is per listening port. Thus, if two daemons are started, one with\n  `{max_sessions,N}` and the other with `{max_sessions,M}`, in total `N+M`\n  connections are accepted for the whole `ssh` application.\n\n  Notice that if `parallel_login` is `false`, only one client at a time can be\n  in the authentication phase.\n\n  By default, this option is not set. This means that the number is not limited.\n\n- **`max_channels`{: #hardening_daemon_options-max_channels }** - The maximum\n  number of channels with active remote subsystem that are accepted for each\n  connection to this daemon\n\n  By default, this option is not set. This means that the number is not limited.\n\n- **`parallel_login`{: #hardening_daemon_options-parallel_login }** - If set to\n  false (the default value), only one login is handled at a time. If set to\n  true, an unlimited number of login attempts are allowed simultaneously.\n\n  If the `max_sessions` option is set to `N` and `parallel_login` is set to\n  `true`, the maximum number of simultaneous login attempts at any time is\n  limited to `N-K`, where `K` is the number of authenticated connections present\n  at this daemon.\n\n  > #### Warning {: .warning }\n  >\n  > Do not enable `parallel_logins` without protecting the server by other\n  > means, for example, by the `max_sessions` option or a firewall\n  > configuration. If set to `true`, there is no protection against DOS attacks.\n\n- **`minimal_remote_max_packet_size`{:\n  #hardening_daemon_options-minimal_remote_max_packet_size }** - The least\n  maximum packet size that the daemon will accept in channel open requests from\n  the client. The default value is 0.\n\"\"\".\n-doc(#{title => <<\"Daemon Options\">>}).\n-type hardening_daemon_options() ::\n        {max_sessions, pos_integer()}\n      | {max_channels, pos_integer()}\n      | {parallel_login, boolean()}\n      | {minimal_remote_max_packet_size, pos_integer()}.\n\n-doc \"\"\"\n- **`connectfun`** - Provides a fun to implement your own logging when a user\n  authenticates to the server.\n\n- **`failfun`** - Provides a fun to implement your own logging when a user fails\n  to authenticate.\n\"\"\".\n-doc(#{title => <<\"Daemon Options\">>}).\n-type callbacks_daemon_options() ::\n        {failfun, fun((User::string(), Peer::{inet:ip_address(), inet:port_number()}, Reason::term()) -> _)}\n      | {connectfun, fun((User::string(), Peer::{inet:ip_address(), inet:port_number()}, Method::string()) ->_)} .\n\n-doc(#{title => <<\"Other data types\">>}).\n-type opaque_daemon_options()  ::\n        {infofun, fun()}\n      | opaque_common_options().\n\n-doc(#{title => <<\"Other data types\">>}).\n-type ip_port() :: {inet:ip_address(), inet:port_number()} .\n\n-doc(#{title => <<\"Other data types\">>}).\n-type mod_args() :: {Module::atom(), Args::list()} .\n-doc(#{title => <<\"Other data types\">>}).\n-type mod_fun_args() :: {Module::atom(), Function::atom(), Args::list()} .\n\n\n%% Records\n-record(address, {address,\n                  port,\n                  profile\n                 }).\n\n-record(ssh,\n\t{\n\t  role :: role(),\n\t  peer :: undefined | \n                  {inet:hostname(),ip_port()},         %% string version of peer address \n\n          local,        %% Local sockname. Need this AFTER a socket is closed by i.e. a crash\n\n\t  c_vsn,        %% client version {Major,Minor}\n\t  s_vsn,        %% server version {Major,Minor}\n\n\t  c_version,    %% client version string\n\t  s_version,    %% server version string\n\n\t  c_keyinit,    %% binary payload of kexinit packet\n\t  s_keyinit,    %% binary payload of kexinit packet\n\n          send_ext_info, %% May send ext-info to peer\n          recv_ext_info, %% Expect ext-info from peer\n\n          kex_strict_negotiated = false,\n\n\t  algorithms,   %% #alg{}\n\t  \n\t  send_mac = none, %% send MAC algorithm\n\t  send_mac_key,  %% key used in send MAC algorithm\n\t  send_mac_size = 0,\n\n\t  recv_mac = none, %% recv MAC algorithm\n\t  recv_mac_key,  %% key used in recv MAC algorithm\n\t  recv_mac_size = 0,\n\n\t  encrypt = none,       %% encrypt algorithm\n          encrypt_cipher,       %% cipher. could be different from the algorithm\n\t  encrypt_keys,         %% encrypt keys\n\t  encrypt_block_size = 8,\n\t  encrypt_ctx,\n\n\t  decrypt = none,       %% decrypt algorithm\n          decrypt_cipher,       %% cipher. could be different from the algorithm\n\t  decrypt_keys,         %% decrypt keys\n\t  decrypt_block_size = 8,\n\t  decrypt_ctx,          %% Decryption context   \n\n\t  compress = none,\n\t  compress_ctx,\n\t  decompress = none,\n\t  decompress_ctx,\n\n\t  c_lng=none,   %% client to server languages\n\t  s_lng=none,   %% server to client languages\n\n\t  user_ack    = true,   %% client\n\t  timeout     = infinity,\n\n\t  shared_secret,        %% K from key exchange\n\t  exchanged_hash,       %% H from key exchange\n\t  session_id,           %% same as FIRST exchanged_hash\n\t  \n\t  opts = [],\n\t  send_sequence = 0,\n\t  recv_sequence = 0,\n\t  keyex_key,\n\t  keyex_info,\n\t  random_length_padding = ?MAX_RND_PADDING_LEN, % From RFC 4253 section 6.\n\t  \n\t  %% User auth\n\t  user,\n\t  service,\n\t  userauth_quiet_mode,              %  boolean()\n\t  userauth_methods,                 %  list( string() )  eg [\"keyboard-interactive\", \"password\"]\n\t  userauth_supported_methods,       %  string() eg \"keyboard-interactive,password\"\n          userauth_pubkeys,\n\t  kb_tries_left = 0,                %  integer(), num tries left for \"keyboard-interactive\"\n\t  userauth_preference,\n\t  available_host_keys,\n\t  pwdfun_user_state,\n\t  authenticated = false\n\t }).\n\n-record(alg,\n\t{\n\t  kex,\n\t  hkey,\n\t  send_mac,\n\t  recv_mac,\n\t  encrypt,\n\t  decrypt,\n\t  compress,\n\t  decompress,\n\t  c_lng,\n\t  s_lng,\n          send_ext_info,\n          recv_ext_info,\n          kex_strict_negotiated = false\n\t }).\n\n-record(ssh_pty, {c_version = \"\", % client version string, ?wr_record(N, [])).\n\n\n%% Circular trace buffer macros\n\n-record(circ_buf_entry,\n        {\n          module,\n          line,\n          function,\n          pid = self(),\n          value\n        }).\n\n-define(CIRC_BUF_IN(VALUE),\n        ssh_dbg:cbuf_in(\n          #circ_buf_entry{module = ?MODULE,\n                          line = ?LINE,\n                          function = %%

%%
%% SSH definitions
%%

-ifndef(SSH_HRL).
-define(SSH_HRL, 1).

-define(SSH_DEFAULT_PORT, 22).
-define(SSH_MAX_PACKET_SIZE, (256*1024)).
-define(REKEY_DATA_TIMOUT, 60000).
-define(DEFAULT_PROFILE, default).

-define(DEFAULT_TRANSPORT,  {tcp, gen_tcp, tcp_closed} ).

-define(DEFAULT_SHELL, {shell, start, []} ).

-define(DEFAULT_TIMEOUT, 5000).

-define(MAX_RND_PADDING_LEN, 15).

-define(SUPPORTED_AUTH_METHODS, "publickey,keyboard-interactive,password").

-define(FALSE, 0).
-define(TRUE,  1).
%% basic binary constructors
-define(BOOLEAN(X),  (X):8/unsigned-big-integer).
-define(BYTE(X),     (X):8/unsigned-big-integer).
-define(UINT16(X),   (X):16/unsigned-big-integer).
-define(UINT32(X),   (X):32/unsigned-big-integer).
-define(UINT64(X),   (X):64/unsigned-big-integer).
-define(STRING(X),   ?UINT32((byte_size(X))), (X)/binary).

-define(DEC_BIN(X,Len),   ?UINT32(Len), X:Len/binary ).
-define(DEC_INT(I,Len),   ?UINT32(Len), I:Len/big-signed-integer-unit:8 ).
-define(DEC_MPINT(I,Len), ?UINT32(Len), I:Len/big-signed-integer-unit:8 ).

%% building macros
-define(boolean(X),
	case X of
	    true -> <<?BOOLEAN(1)>>;
	    false -> (<<?BOOLEAN(0)>>)
	end).

-define(byte(X),   << ?BYTE(X) >> ).
-define(uint16(X), << ?UINT16(X) >> ).
-define(uint32(X), << ?UINT32(X) >> ).
-define(uint64(X), << ?UINT64(X) >> ).
-define(string_utf8(X), << ?STRING(unicode:characters_to_binary(X)) >> ).
-define(string(X), ?string_utf8(X)).
-define(binary(X), << ?STRING(X) >>).

-define('2bin'(X), (if is_binary(X) -> X;
		       is_list(X) -> list_to_binary(X);
		       X==undefined -> <<>>
		    end) ).

%% encoding macros
-define('E...'(X),    ?'2bin'(X)/binary ).
-define(Eboolean(X),  ?BOOLEAN(case X of
				   true -> ?TRUE;
				   false -> ?FALSE
			       end) ).
-define(Ebyte(X),        ?BYTE(X) ).
-define(Euint32(X),      ?UINT32(X) ).
-define(Estring(X),      ?STRING(?'2bin'(X)) ).
-define(Estring_utf8(X), ?string_utf8(X)/binary ).
-define(Ename_list(X),   ?STRING(ssh_bits:name_list(X)) ).
-define(Empint(X),       (ssh_bits:mpint(X))/binary ).
-define(Ebinary(X),      ?STRING(X) ).

%% Other macros
-define(to_binary(X), (try iolist_to_binary(X) catch _:_ -> unicode:characters_to_binary(X) end) ).

%% Cipher details
-define(SSH_CIPHER_NONE, 0).
-define(SSH_CIPHER_3DES, 3).
-define(SSH_CIPHER_AUTHFILE, ?SSH_CIPHER_3DES).

%% Option access macros
-define(do_get_opt(C,K,O),   ssh_options:get_value(C,K,O,  ?MODULE,?LINE)).
-define(do_get_opt(C,K,O,D), ssh_options:get_value(C,K,O,?LAZY(D),?MODULE,?LINE)).

-define(LAZY(D), fun()-> D end).

-define(GET_OPT(Key,Opts),              ?do_get_opt(user_options,    Key,Opts    ) ).
-define(GET_OPT(Key,Opts,Def),          ?do_get_opt(user_options,    Key,Opts,Def) ).
-define(GET_INTERNAL_OPT(Key,Opts),     ?do_get_opt(internal_options,Key,Opts    ) ).
-define(GET_INTERNAL_OPT(Key,Opts,Def), ?do_get_opt(internal_options,Key,Opts,Def) ).
-define(GET_SOCKET_OPT(Key,Opts),       ?do_get_opt(socket_options,  Key,Opts    ) ).
-define(GET_SOCKET_OPT(Key,Opts,Def),   ?do_get_opt(socket_options,  Key,Opts,Def) ).

-define(do_put_opt(C,KV,O),  ssh_options:put_value(C,KV,O, ?MODULE,?LINE)).

-define(PUT_OPT(KeyVal,Opts),           ?do_put_opt(user_options,    KeyVal,Opts) ).
-define(PUT_INTERNAL_OPT(KeyVal,Opts),  ?do_put_opt(internal_options,KeyVal,Opts) ).
-define(PUT_SOCKET_OPT(KeyVal,Opts),    ?do_put_opt(socket_options,  KeyVal,Opts) ).

-define(do_del_opt(C,K,O),  ssh_options:delete_key(C,K,O, ?MODULE,?LINE)).
-define(DELETE_INTERNAL_OPT(Key,Opts),  ?do_del_opt(internal_options,Key,Opts) ).


%% Types
-type role()                  :: client | server .

-doc(#{title => <<"Other data types">>}).
-type host()                  :: string() | inet:ip_address() | loopback .
-doc """
The socket is supposed to be result of a [gen_tcp:connect](`gen_tcp:connect/3`)
or a [gen_tcp:accept](`gen_tcp:accept/1`). The socket must be in passive mode
(that is, opened with the option `{active,false})`.
""".
-doc(#{title => <<"Other data types">>}).
-type open_socket()           :: gen_tcp:socket().

-doc """
Defines a subsystem in the daemon.

The `subsystem_name` is the name that a client requests to start with for
example `ssh_connection:subsystem/4`.

The `channel_callback` is the module that implements the `m:ssh_server_channel`
(replaces ssh_daemon_channel) behaviour in the daemon. See the section
[Creating a Subsystem](using_ssh.md#usersguide_creating_a_subsystem) in the
User's Guide for more information and an example.

If the subsystems option is not present, the value of
`ssh_sftpd:subsystem_spec([])` is used. This enables the sftp subsystem by
default. The option can be set to the empty list if you do not want the daemon
to run any subsystems.
""".
-doc(#{title => <<"Daemon Options">>}).
-type subsystem_spec()        :: {Name::string(), mod_args()} .
                              
-doc(#{title => <<"Common Options">>}).
-type algs_list()             :: list( alg_entry() ).
-doc(#{title => <<"Common Options">>}).
-type alg_entry()             :: {kex, [kex_alg()]} 
                               | {public_key, [pubkey_alg()]}
                               | {cipher, double_algs(cipher_alg())}
                               | {mac, double_algs(mac_alg())}
                               | {compression, double_algs(compression_alg())} .

-doc(#{title => <<"Common Options">>}).
-type kex_alg()          :: 'curve25519-sha256' |
                            'curve25519-sha256@libssh.org' |
                            'curve448-sha512' |
                            'ecdh-sha2-nistp521' |
                            'ecdh-sha2-nistp384' |
                            'ecdh-sha2-nistp256' |
                            'diffie-hellman-group-exchange-sha256' |
                            'diffie-hellman-group16-sha512' |
                            'diffie-hellman-group18-sha512' |
                            'diffie-hellman-group14-sha256' |
                            'diffie-hellman-group14-sha1' |
                            'diffie-hellman-group-exchange-sha1' |
                            'diffie-hellman-group1-sha1'
                            .

-doc(#{title => <<"Common Options">>}).
-type pubkey_alg()       :: 'ssh-ed25519' |
                            'ssh-ed448' |
                            'ecdsa-sha2-nistp521' |
                            'ecdsa-sha2-nistp384' |
                            'ecdsa-sha2-nistp256' |
                            'rsa-sha2-512' |
                            'rsa-sha2-256' |
                            'ssh-rsa' |
                            'ssh-dss'
                            .

-doc(#{title => <<"Common Options">>}).
-type cipher_alg()       :: 'aes256-gcm@openssh.com' |
                            'aes256-ctr' |
                            'aes192-ctr' |
                            'aes128-gcm@openssh.com' |
                            'aes128-ctr' |
                            'AEAD_AES_256_GCM' |
                            'AEAD_AES_128_GCM' |
                            'chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com' |
                            'aes256-cbc' |
                            'aes192-cbc' |
                            'aes128-cbc' |
                            '3des-cbc'
                            .

-doc(#{title => <<"Common Options">>}).
-type mac_alg()          :: 'hmac-sha2-512-etm@openssh.com' |
                            'hmac-sha2-256-etm@openssh.com' |
                            'hmac-sha2-512' |
                            'hmac-sha2-256' |
                            'hmac-sha1-etm@openssh.com' |
                            'hmac-sha1' |
                            'hmac-sha1-96' |
                            'AEAD_AES_256_GCM' |
                            'AEAD_AES_128_GCM'
                            .

-doc(#{title => <<"Common Options">>}).
-type compression_alg()  :: 'none' |
                            'zlib' |
                            'zlib@openssh.com'
                            .

-doc """
List of algorithms to use in the algorithm negotiation. The default
`t:algs_list/0` can be obtained from `default_algorithms/0`.

If an alg_entry() is missing in the algs_list(), the default value is used for
that entry.

Here is an example of this option:

```erlang
	  {preferred_algorithms,
	  [{public_key,['ssh-rsa','ssh-dss']},
	  {cipher,[{client2server,['aes128-ctr']},
          {server2client,['aes128-cbc','3des-cbc']}]},
	  {mac,['hmac-sha2-256','hmac-sha1']},
	  {compression,[none,zlib]}
	  ]
	  }
```

The example specifies different algorithms in the two directions (client2server
and server2client), for cipher but specifies the same algorithms for mac and
compression in both directions. The kex (key exchange) is implicit but
public_key is set explicitly.

For background and more examples see the
[User's Guide](configure_algos.md#introduction).

If an algorithm name occurs more than once in a list, the behaviour is
undefined. The tags in the property lists are also assumed to occur at most one
time.

> #### Warning {: .warning }
>
> Changing the values can make a connection less secure. Do not change unless
> you know exactly what you are doing. If you do not understand the values then
> you are not supposed to change them.
""".
-doc(#{title => <<"Common Options">>}).
-type double_algs(AlgType)  :: list( {client2server,[AlgType]} | {server2client,[AlgType]} )
                             | [AlgType].

-doc """
Modifies the list of algorithms to use in the algorithm negotiation. The
modifications are applied after the option `preferred_algorithms` (if existing)
is applied.

The algorithm for modifications works like this:

- Input is the `t:modify_algs_list/0` and a set of algorithms `A` obtained from
  the `preferred_algorithms` option if existing, or else from the
  [ssh:default_algorithms/0](`default_algorithms/0`).
- The head of the `t:modify_algs_list/0` modifies `A` giving the result `A'`.

  The possible modifications are:

  - Append or prepend supported but not enabled algorithm(s) to the list of
    algorithms. If the wanted algorithms already are in `A` they will first be
    removed and then appended or prepended,
  - Remove (rm) one or more algorithms from `A`.

- Repeat the modification step with the tail of `t:modify_algs_list/0` and the
  resulting `A'`.

If an unsupported algorithm is in the `t:modify_algs_list/0`, it will be
silently ignored

If there are more than one modify_algorithms options, the result is undefined.

Here is an example of this option:

```text
	  {modify_algorithms,
	  [{prepend, [{kex, ['diffie-hellman-group1-sha1']}],
	  {rm,      [{compression, [none]}]}
	  ]
	  }
```

The example specifies that:

- the old key exchange algorithm 'diffie-hellman-group1-sha1' should be the main
  alternative. It will be the main alternative since it is prepened to the list
- The compression algorithm none (= no compression) is removed so compression is
  enforced

For background and more examples see the
[User's Guide](configure_algos.md#introduction).
""".
-doc(#{title => <<"Common Options">>}).
-type modify_algs_list()      :: list( {append,algs_list()} | {prepend,algs_list()} | {rm,algs_list()} ) .

-type internal_options()      :: ssh_options:private_options().
-type socket_options()        :: [gen_tcp:connect_option() | gen_tcp:listen_option()].

-doc(#{title => <<"Client Options">>}).
-type client_options()        :: [ client_option() ] .
-doc(#{title => <<"Daemon Options">>}).
-type daemon_options()        :: [ daemon_option() ].

-doc(#{title => <<"Common Options">>}).
-type common_options() :: [ common_option() ].
-doc """
The options above can be used both in clients and in daemons (servers). They are
further explained below.
""".
-doc(#{title => <<"Common Options">>}).
-type common_option() ::
        ssh_file:user_dir_common_option()
      | profile_common_option()
      | max_idle_time_common_option()
      | max_log_item_len_common_option()
      | key_cb_common_option()
      | disconnectfun_common_option()
      | unexpectedfun_common_option()
      | ssh_msg_debug_fun_common_option()
      | rekey_limit_common_option()
      | id_string_common_option()
      | pref_public_key_algs_common_option()
      | preferred_algorithms_common_option()
      | modify_algorithms_common_option()
      | auth_methods_common_option()
      | inet_common_option()
      | fd_common_option()
        .

-define(COMMON_OPTION, common_option()).

-doc """
Used together with `ip-address` and `port` to uniquely identify a ssh daemon.
This can be useful in a virtualized environment, where there can be more that
one server that has the same `ip-address` and `port`. If this property is not
explicitly set, it is assumed that the the `ip-address` and `port` uniquely
identifies the SSH daemon.
""".
-doc(#{title => <<"Common Options">>}).
-type profile_common_option()       :: {profile,   atom() }.
-doc """
Sets a time-out on a connection when no channels are open. Defaults to
`infinity`. The unit is milliseconds.

The timeout is not active until channels are started, so it does not limit the
time from the connection creation to the first channel opening.

For more information about timeouts, see the
[Timeouts section ](hardening.md#timeouts)in the User's Guide
[Hardening](hardening.md) chapter.
""".
-doc(#{title => <<"Common Options">>}).
-type max_idle_time_common_option() :: {idle_time, timeout()}.
-doc(#{title => <<"Common Options">>}).
-type rekey_limit_common_option()   :: {rekey_limit, Bytes::limit_bytes() |
                                                     {Minutes::limit_time(), Bytes::limit_bytes()}
                                       }.
-doc """
Sets a limit for the size of a logged item excluding a header. The unit is bytes
and the value defaults to 500.
""".
-doc(#{title => <<"Common Options">>}).
-type max_log_item_len_common_option() :: {max_log_item_len, limit_bytes()} .

-doc(#{title => <<"Common Options">>}).
-type limit_bytes() :: non_neg_integer() | infinity .  % non_neg_integer due to compatibility
-doc """
Sets the limit when rekeying is to be initiated. Both the max time and max
amount of data could be configured:

- `{Minutes, Bytes}` initiate rekeying when any of the limits are reached.
- `Bytes` initiate rekeying when `Bytes` number of bytes are transferred, or at
  latest after one hour.

When a rekeying is done, both the timer and the byte counter are restarted.
Defaults to one hour and one GByte.

If `Minutes` is set to `infinity`, no rekeying will ever occur due to that max
time has passed. Setting `Bytes` to `infinity` will inhibit rekeying after a
certain amount of data has been transferred. If the option value is set to
`{infinity, infinity}`, no rekeying will be initiated. Note that rekeying
initiated by the peer will still be performed.
""".
-doc(#{title => <<"Common Options">>}).
-type limit_time()  :: pos_integer() | infinity .

-doc """
Module implementing the behaviour `m:ssh_client_key_api` and/or
`m:ssh_server_key_api`. Can be used to customize the handling of public keys. If
callback options are provided along with the module name, they are made
available to the callback module via the options passed to it under the key
'key_cb_private'.

The `Opts` defaults to `[]` when only the `Module` is specified.

The default value of this option is `{ssh_file, []}`. See also the manpage of
`m:ssh_file`.

A call to the call-back function `F` will be

```text
	  Module:F(..., [{key_cb_private,Opts}|UserOptions])
```

where `...` are arguments to `F` as in `m:ssh_client_key_api` and/or
`m:ssh_server_key_api`. The `UserOptions` are the options given to
[ssh:connect](`connect/3`), [ssh:shell](`shell/1`) or [ssh:daemon](`daemon/2`).
""".
-doc(#{title => <<"Common Options">>}).
-type key_cb_common_option()            :: {key_cb,  Module::atom() | {Module::atom(),Opts::[term()]} } .
-doc "Provides a fun to implement your own logging or other handling at disconnects.".
-doc(#{title => <<"Common Options">>}).
-type disconnectfun_common_option()     ::
        {disconnectfun, fun((Reason::term()) -> void | any()) }.
-doc """
Provides a fun to implement your own logging or other action when an unexpected
message arrives. If the fun returns `report` the usual info report is issued but
if `skip` is returned no report is generated.
""".
-doc(#{title => <<"Common Options">>}).
-type unexpectedfun_common_option()     ::
        {unexpectedfun, fun((Message::term(),{Host::term(),Port::term()}) -> report | skip ) }.
-doc """
Provide a fun to implement your own logging of the SSH message SSH_MSG_DEBUG.
The last three parameters are from the message, see
[RFC 4253, section 11.3](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc4253#section-11.3). The
`t:connection_ref/0` is the reference to the connection on which the message
arrived. The return value from the fun is not checked.

The default behaviour is ignore the message. To get a printout for each message
with `AlwaysDisplay = true`, use for example
`{ssh_msg_debug_fun, fun(_,true,M,_)-> io:format("DEBUG: ~p~n", [M]) end}`
""".
-doc(#{title => <<"Common Options">>}).
-type ssh_msg_debug_fun_common_option() ::
        {ssh_msg_debug_fun, fun((ssh:connection_ref(),AlwaysDisplay::boolean(),Msg::binary(),LanguageTag::binary()) -> any()) } .

-doc """
The string the daemon will present to a connecting peer initially. The default
value is "Erlang/VSN" where VSN is the ssh application version number.

The value `random` will cause a random string to be created at each connection
attempt. This is to make it a bit more difficult for a malicious peer to find
the ssh software brand and version.

The value `{random, Nmin, Nmax}` will make a random string with at least `Nmin`
characters and at most `Nmax` characters.
""".
-doc(#{title => <<"Common Options">>}).
-type id_string_common_option()           :: {id_string,  string() | random | {random,Nmin::pos_integer(),Nmax::pos_integer()} }.
-doc """
List of user (client) public key algorithms to try to use.

The default value is the `public_key` entry in the list returned by
[ssh:default_algorithms/0](`default_algorithms/0`).

If there is no public key of a specified type available, the corresponding entry
is ignored. Note that the available set is dependent on the underlying cryptolib
and current user's public keys.

See also the option [`user_dir`](`t:ssh_file:user_dir_common_option/0`) for
specifying the path to the user's keys.
""".
-doc(#{title => <<"Common Options">>}).
-type pref_public_key_algs_common_option() :: {pref_public_key_algs, [pubkey_alg()] } .
-doc(#{title => <<"Common Options">>}).
